details: _gate takes os.path.basename(gate), requires GATE_NAME (^<40 hex>.gate.log$) and reads only
<wt>/.relay/checks/<name>. The judge base (synced into every project's checker) still promises a runner log or a
pipeline gate for projects without relay's gate. Since the counts are now derived and the gate problems are N findings,
those projects can never record open 0. CONFIRMED (reproduced). Size: 30.
evidence: scratch log refused: nothing recorded: `gate` must be "none" or a <sha>.gate.log file name, got '/private/var/.../gate.log'
pipeline refused: nothing recorded: `gate` must be "none" or a <sha>.gate.log file name, got 'pipeline #12 on 13b15f99... passed'
git show master:lib/relay_verdict.py:195  gate must be a log path or null   (any path accepted before)
roles/judge.md:120 and plugins/delegate/skills/delegate/SKILL.md:108-112 name runner logs and pipelines as gates.
failing_case: A project without .relay/ (the delegate skill step 3: "Elsewhere the gate is the project's own command, run by a runner
into a log"), or one whose gate is a remote pipeline (judge step 2: "Gate: pipeline #<n> on <full sha> passed").
The checker writes gate = "<scratchpad>/gate.log" (first line head <sha>, last exit 0) or gate = "pipeline #12 on <sha> passed".
Now: `relay check record check` refuses: gate must be "none" or a <sha>.gate.log file name. Writing gate = "none" instead
records N1 HIGH "no gate result for the code of this change", so open is 1 on every check of every such project.
Before this change master accepted any gate text (relay_verdict.py record_errors: "gate must be a log path or null").
Expected: a green log at any path whose first line is head <checked code> and last line exit 0, or a passed pipeline line
for that sha, records with no N finding and open 0.
fix_hint: In _gate: accept a path (absolute or relative to the worktree) and read the log there; keep the head/exit/later-change
checks; accept "pipeline #<n> on <sha> passed" as a gate whose sha follows the same later-change rule. The mark keeps
only a gate under .relay/checks (write_mark already checks the file exists there).
pass_cases: 1. gate = "<scratch>/gate.log" holding "head <HEAD>" ... "exit 0", code unchanged since: recorded, no N finding, open 0.
2. gate = "pipeline #12 on <HEAD> passed": recorded, no N finding (record keeps the line or a pipeline field).
3. gate = "<wt>/.relay/checks/<HEAD>.gate.log" green (today's relay case): recorded, gate = its name, no N (works today).
4. the same scratch log ending "exit 1": recorded with N1 "the gate is red", open 1.
5. a scratch log whose head is an older commit with code changed since: N1 "for other code than head".
findings.summary: a check can no longer name a gate that is not <wt>/.relay/checks/<sha>.gate.log: runner logs and remote pipelines are refused, and `none` adds an open HIGH

details: _gate("none") takes base = merge-base(default, head) and relay_inert.changed(wt, base, head) without own=True, so the
whole change (and anything a merge from the default branch brought) counts as "code changed with no gate". The judge
text keeps the exemption for a review with no fix commits and for openspec/ and docs files; the script now adds the N
finding itself and the checker cannot answer it (N findings take no status). In the issues flow every review with
nothing to fix ends with open 1. CONFIRMED (reproduced). Size: 20.
evidence: fixes-none open 1 [('N1', 'no gate result for the code of this change')]
artifacts open 1 [('N1', 'no gate result for the code of this change')]
git show master:roles/judge.md step 2: "Otherwise a missing log (with fix commits), a red one, or one for other code is open +1".
failing_case: plugins/issues/skills/implement/SKILL.md:62 (and checker.md:16): "with no fix commits, `Fixes: none` and `Gate: none`".
A branch changed lib/y.py; the review is of HEAD and found only a LOW; no fix follows. The checker records gate = "none"
and MET for every finding.
Now: the record gets N1 HIGH "no gate result for the code of this change", open 1, because _gate lists every non-inert
file changed since the merge-base with the default branch, the whole change, not the fix commits.
Old rule (judge text on master): "a missing log (with fix commits) ... is open +1"; with no fix commit nothing counted.
Expected: no N finding and open 0 when no own non-inert file changed after the newest review's since.
fix_hint: In _gate's "none" branch: list relay_inert.changed(wt, <newest review since>, head, own=True) (build_findings already has
the reviews' since), drop openspec/** and docs/**, and add the N finding only when something is left.
pass_cases: 1. review of HEAD, no commit after it, gate "none": no N finding, open 0.
2. review of the take commit, a fix commit to lib/y.py after it, gate "none": N1 "no gate result", open 1 (works today).
3. review of HEAD, then only docs/handover.md or .relay/ commits, gate "none": no N finding.
4. review of HEAD, then a merge of the default branch bringing only master's files, gate "none": no N finding (own files only).
5. review of HEAD, then only openspec/** or docs/** changed, gate "none": no N finding (the judge text's exemption, step 2).
findings.summary: Gate: none with Fixes: none records an open HIGH 'no gate result' for every code change, though no fix commit came after the review

details: build_findings sets the anchors to the newest mark on the branch's own commits and the reviews' since; _merge_findings
only looks at merges in anchor..head. A mark is written for every check, also one with open > 0, so a NOT MET M of that
check is before the anchor of the next one. F findings survive because the review files are passed again; M findings
have no file to be passed again. The design text says "the newer of the branch's last mark and the newest F since",
but its intent (the merge check, one checker run) is to judge each combination; the fix stays inside the design by
taking the newest mark whose record holds no M that is not MET (or open 0). CONFIRMED (reproduced). Size: 20.
failing_case: The branch is reviewed, takes master (master changed lib/y.py, which the branch also changed), gate, check 1: M1 NOT MET,
open 1, mark written. The owner says fix it; the fixer commits lib/w.py (not y.py); gate; check 2 with Q1 and F1 MET.
Now: check 2's record holds only Q1 and F1 (no M1), open 0, so the merge goes on with the merge combination never MET.
Expected: M1 is listed again (or open stays above 0) until a check gives it MET.
fix_hint: In build_findings, pick as the mark anchor the newest own mark whose stored record has every M finding MET (read with
relay_marks.check_data); a record with an M not MET does not move the anchor.
pass_cases: 1. Check 1 has M1 NOT MET; a fix that does not touch the file; check 2: `relay check findings` lists M1 again and the record needs its verdict.
2. Check 1 has M1 MET; check 2 after more fixes and no new merge: no M finding (works today).
3. Check 1 with no M; a later merge of the default branch changes a file the branch changed: M1 at that merge (works today).
4. Check 1 has M1 NOT MET, then a new merge brings another file: check 2 lists both files.
findings.summary: an M finding judged NOT MET disappears from the next check: the anchor is the last mark, whatever its verdicts
